Higgs_sequestering.closed_zero_portal_condition: For each real sector: y=0 or all three source Yukawa coefficients e=t=a=0
Higgs_sequestering.normalization: 16*pi^2 coefficients, H^dagger H multiplying source quadratics
Higgs_sequestering.scope: Zero portals and arbitrary source quartics: Higgs and source scalar sectors have no shared scalar-loop product. Fermion boxes alone necessarily generate the displayed portals for nonzero Higgs and source Yukawas. Additional fields or interactions can change this result.
Higgs_sequestering.sequestered_resummed_theorem: If no scalar mass eigenmode has both Higgs and source vertices, the corrected top mass block is a Hermitian function of C. Its determinant ratio is positive when the correction norm is below one.

conclusion: Finite Gaussian scalar exchange correlates derivative terms and exact pole residues. First-order mass-phase reality does not imply reality of the resummed one-loop determinant; exact Higgs sequestering would protect that restricted determinant but is not closed under the specified nonzero Yukawa running.

exact_Gaussian_wall_bridge.scope: Exact conditional Gaussian wall sandwich and fully classified dimensionless two-field example; not the quark flavor vacuum or a cosmological normalization.

exact_gaussian_certificate.scope: The displayed nonlocal sign uses a mostly-minus Minkowski Lagrangian; the static effective potential is -J^2/(2 M^2). General matrix identity follows by Schur complement.
